keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no row; the area sits in its Lithuania and Second Polish Republic shapes). Infobox area 13,490 km2; the 60 km disc round Vilnius resolves to about 13,000 km2 (ratio about 1.0). The page names no town but Vilnius ('Vilnius and its region'), so the disc is the researcher's reading (confidence 2); the page says all of the Republic's territory later went into the Wilno Voivodeship. FIX PASS 1 Nov 2026 (extent, after the review's thin remark that the real state reached Lida, Braslaw and Švenčionys): the Republic page names no town but Vilnius and none of those; its infobox area (13,490 km2, no year) matches the 60 km disc, so the disc stays. The Wilno Voivodeship page (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilno_Voivodeship_(1926%E2%80%931939)) gives the voivodeship 29,011 km2 and nine counties (Braslaw, Dzisna, Molodechno, Oshmyany, Pastavy, Švenčionys, Vileyka, Vilnius-Trakai, Vilnius City), says the territory 'was known as the Wilno Land' from 6 April 1922 and that the voivodeship was created on 20 January 1926; its Mołodeczno county dates from 1 April 1927. That is a later, 2.15 times larger unit than the Republic, so it gives no admin units for the Republic itself and was not used; second-polish-republic's 100 km disc (32,250 km2) is the nearer match to the voivodeship, not to this state. The three discs (47, 60, 100 km) remain for the compiler to reconcile: this dossier's 60 km is the only one tied to the Republic's own area figure.

ledger.note: 12 October 1920: Żeligowski proclaims the Republic of Central Lithuania at Vilnius. 'It was founded on 12 October 1920, after the successful Żeligowski Mutiny'; his forces set out on 8 October and entered Vilnius on 9 October (Mutiny page: 'On October 12, Żeligowski proclaimed the independence of the area'), a 'puppet state of the Second Polish Republic' (infobox).

region.text: the Republic's territory, 'Vilnius and its region'

ledger.note: 12 October 1920: the new state is a puppet of Poland from its founding. The Republic page: infobox 'Status: Puppet state of the Second Polish Republic'; lead 'an unrecognized short-lived puppet state of Poland, that existed from 1920 to 1922'; 'it was an imitation of a sovereign state'. 'Poland disclaimed all responsibility for the action, maintaining that Żeligowski had acted entirely on his own initiative', yet Piłsudski later admitted 'the attack was undertaken by his direct order'. The page has no phrase about 'Polish protection'. Mirrors second-polish-republic/ledger/11 (1920 vassal_start, counterpart central-lithuania, the same 60 km disc).

region.text: Giedraičiai, Širvintos and Kėdainiai, the targets of Żeligowski's advance

ledger.note: 7 November 1920: Żeligowski's army advances beyond Vilnius. 'On 7 November, Żeligowski's army advanced toward Giedraičiai, Širvintos, and Kėdainiai'; on 18 November Polish cavalry 'reached Kavarskas'; from 19 to 21 November the Lithuanians pushed them back near Giedraičiai and Širvintos. The disc is the researcher's reading of the Širvintos-Giedraičiai front.

21 November 1920: the ceasefire takes effect. 'A ceasefire was negotiated on 20 November with League of Nations help, and it was to take effect on 21 November 1920 at 9 a.m.'; a truce was signed on 29 November. The Republic page also has the League mediating and the talks at Suwałki.

22 March 1922: the vassalage ends with incorporation into Poland. The Republic page: 'The request was accepted by the Polish Sejm on 22 March 1922' (text) and 'Incorporation into Poland: 18 April 1922' (infobox); second-polish-republic/ledger/20 dates the end 24 March 1922 from another page. Mirrors that line (1922/3 vassal_end, counterpart central-lithuania); the dissolve below carries the same month.

region.text: the Republic, incorporated into Poland and the Wilno Voivodeship

ledger.note: March 1922: Central Lithuania is incorporated into Poland. The Republic's Sejm 'on February 20 passed the request of incorporation into Poland' after a disputed election on 8 January 1922; the Polish Sejm accepted it on 22 March 1922 (infobox: incorporation 18 April 1922; second-polish-republic gives 24 March 1922 from another page). Lithuania did not recognise the border until 1938.

wars.name: Żeligowski's Mutiny

zones.text: Vilnius and its region, taken on 8-9 October 1920

wars.outcome: Żeligowski's forces, secretly ordered by Piłsudski, took Vilnius on 9 October and proclaimed Central Lithuania on 12 October; the Lithuanians held at Giedraičiai and Širvintos in 19-21 November and a ceasefire took effect on 21 November, a truce on 29 November.
wars.note: The Mutiny page: Piłsudski 'surreptitiously ordered Żeligowski to carry out the operation'; the Polish government officially denied involvement. The ceasefire date (21 November) and truce (29 November) are the page's; the Republic page mixes them (ceasefire 21 November, truce six days later).

certainty.note: A puppet state with no treaty frontier; Lithuania refused to recognise the line, which the Conference of Ambassadors accepted in 1923 (page: recognised 'during the interwar period'). The Širvintos front moved week by week in November 1920.
